title: Tech guy trying to get into trading ,1.5 months in and I’m somehow losing money faster than I can learn 😭 What am I missing?
author: unbothered_ndchalant
selftext:
I'm a tech person trying to learn trading and hopefully make even a small side income from it.

For the past 1.5 months I've built and deployed multiple trading bots. So far mostly losses. I'm also paying for APIs, cloud usage, model credits, etc.

I've been paper trading and made around $6. I've tried 15+ strategies generated/backtested with AI, but I feel like I'm just jumping from one strategy to another without actually understanding what I'm doing.

I can code and build the systems, but I don't really understand trading yet.

If you were starting from zero as a technical person, where would you start?

Should I forget bots for now and learn trading manually? Focus on one strategy? Learn statistics/quant stuff? Something else?

I'm not looking for a get-rich-quick strategy. I just want a proper path to actually learn this instead of wasting more money and blindly asking AI to generate strategies.

Any advice is appreciated, especially from people who started out similarly.

replies.author: BrandonDogDad
replies.body:
I traded for a few years and always lost money but always got better. Then I put it on pause and got back into it about a year and a half ago. I spent the last year building solid training pipelines on ES and NQ. I’ve tested thousands of strategies and used a lot of different methods like Markov, HMM, I’ve scoured hundreds of academic papers and mathematic papers to find edges in the market. 

It all boiled down to about 15 strategies that were PROFITABLE on everything I threw at it, fully back tested and tested on out of sample data. They ran love for about 4 months. Some printed money. 3-4K per day on a single contract. The issue that occurs over and over is regime change. You can build a phenomenal strategy, but then when something like Covid, tariff, or Iran war starts, your strategy… All of them actually will stop working.

 I’ve since put the bots on hold and used AI to do statistic analysis on a bunch of other market related items and now have been using AI to build me custom indicators to visualize what’s happening in the market and that has helped me do quite well with manual trading. If it were easy, everybody would be doing it. 

There is a reason why it may take years to finally crack but once you do, you can make an astronomical amount of money, but it likely won’t happen quickly, which I know is the answer You probably don’t want to hear, but it’s the truth.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: You're doing the classic engineer thing: building the system before you understand the problem. 15 strategies in 1.5 months means you're not actually testing anything, you're just curve fitting and moving on when it breaks. Forget the bots for now. Pick one instrument, one timeframe, and trade it manually on paper for a few months until you can explain why you're entering and exiting without an algorithm telling you. The coding skills are a huge advantage later, but right now they're letting you skip the part where you actually learn what moves price.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Fifteen strategies in six weeks is the problem, not the missing trading knowledge. Each one got about three days, which is not long enough to teach you anything about any of them, and that churn is what is eating the API money.

I would keep the bots and drop the strategy hunt. Take one idea and spend two weeks making the backtest honest instead of making the idea better. AI-generated backtests break the same few ways every time: deciding on a bar's close and filling at that same close, filling at the touch price with no spread, a symbol list chosen because those names already worked, and an exit target that was tuned on the sample. Fix those four and most beautiful curves go flat, which is useful information rather than a setback.

The statistics worth learning first is just sample size. A result on 12 or 20 trades is not distinguishable from luck, which is probably true of most of the 15.

comments.author: Finallytherenow
comments.body:
This might sound outlandish and or outright bull$hit. If so, please excuse my intrusion. 

It is my belief the US Equity Markets are rigged agains retail Traders. I say this because this has been my experience trading over 35 years with Discount Shops.  Most retail are subjugated to trading with Discount Brokerages because they have the biggest psychological act in town; Free Trades.  

These Discount shops provide free trading for US Stocks.   They do this by betting against their own clients, in effect writing an IOU against what their clients purchase on their platforms believing their clients will eventually end up selling at a loss.  Yes, they believe 90+% Retail loses money on their trades. Think about that.  90% lose $'s trading stocks.  So they bet against you.

Sounds crazy ?  Yup, I get that.  But I believe it to be true.  When you buy shares through these Discount Shops they hold your shares in 'Street Name', which gives them full control of the shares you believe you own. They can Short against, and often do, and or loan out your shares to other entities. They can even choose not to buy your shares but provide an IOU, time stamped, for your exact executed trade. You think you have bought the actual shares but in essence only bought an IOU from your Discount Broker.  All of this is predicated on the exact type of Company shares you Buy. Dividend Stocks are actually purchased but only in street name.  Cheaper Stocks with no Dividends are likely not purchased but rather given an IOU.  All this gives these discount brokers extreme leverage over your shares and your chances of succeeding on their platforms.   

If you are of the mindset to Buy and hold your brokers know this as well and limit implementing these nefarious activities.  Also, you are subjugated to Binding Arbitration should a discrepancy arise.

  
This is what I believe to be true.  

You have to decide for yourself what is true or not.

comments.author: PilotPhysical9616
comments.body:
I like to learn bots lol (but maybe not yet). I purely do manual trades seen lots of bots discord communities running them though. 

1.5 months is really short to learn trading and become profitable. Since you are automating you can backtest larger data (but most aren't free). 

 Personally I would first just learn a strategy figure out what's its edge and why it works first. Automation only comes second (once you find the edge exists). 

The only other difficult thing i would say is some traders do discretionary trading instead. Where fixed mechanical rules may deviate (not always just some strategies I have seen). More systematic strategies would benefit from the automation so filtering for that be one of the later things you can do.
